value: orients away from low-frequency pulsed sound (100-800 Hz bands) from at least 62 m; behavioural response, not a threshold
method: free-ranging sharks filmed from a drone hovering about 40-50 m above an anchored boat (2-5 m of water) while an underwater loudspeaker (suspended 1 m below the surface, 13-19 m off the stern) played, one randomly chosen stimulus per trial, amplitude-modulated pulse trains of filtered noise band-passed 100-200, 200-400 or 400-800 Hz at 140 dB re 1 uPa at 1 m; a response was a sudden change in trajectory starting at stimulus onset; response distance from speaker to snout in the frame before the turn; sound pressure levels measured in situ with hydrophones and propagation modelled
conditions: wild sharks off Southeast Florida near the Jupiter Beach, Palm Beach or Pompano Beach inlets, 07:30-12:30 on low-wind days, no chum or bait mentioned, trial dates not given, no individual identification described (the same shark may have been tested more than once); 209 experimental presentations (72, 54, 83 per band) gave 165 responses (59, 47, 59); each trial began with 5 s of a 10 kHz pulsed control, then 5 s of silence, then the stimulus; the Synopsis also prints that sharks never responded to the 10 kHz control of comparable volume; mean response distance 40.7 m (SD 10.69, range 15.0-74.0 m), 41.0 m (SD 15.56, range 12.4-66.1 m) and 30.0 m (SD 12.81, range 11.1-61.8 m) for the three bands, with the 400-800 Hz mean lower than the other two (ANOVA F = 15.014, P < 0.001; the two lower bands did not differ, Scheffe P = 0.887); the sound pressure level eliciting a response rose with frequency (about 16.0, 27.8 and 44.6 dB relative to peak ambient, ANOVA F = 247.17, P < 0.001), so the shark responded from further away at lower frequency and needed a higher level at higher frequency; turn change 77.3, 66.6 and 72.2 degrees did not differ among bands (ANOVA F = 2.060, P = 0.133); the Synopsis prints 71.6% of responses (n = 209) in the far field while the Results print 71.5% of the 165 responses, and 209 is the count of presentations, so that figure is not used here; far field defined as beyond 3 lambda of the lowest frequency in each band

source.authors: C L Sullivan, E R Gerstein, S M Kajiura
source.title: Orientation of Blacktip Sharks (Carcharhinus limbatus) to Underwater Sound

quote: Sharks responded to all frequencies from at least 62 m, and 71.6% of all responses (n = 209) occurred in the far field.
